about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Rich Brown Beef Stock from Roasted Bones
recipes.summary: A deep, glossy brown stock from well-roasted beef bones and vegetables, the base for gravies and French onion soup.
steps: Roast the bones at 230°C for 45 minutes, turning once, until deep brown.
Smear the vegetables with the tomato paste and roast them alongside for the last 25 minutes until caramelised.
Tip everything into a large pot with the bay and peppercorns and cover with the cold water.
Bring to a bare simmer, skim well, then cook gently uncovered for 5 hours until the stock is rich and brown.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool quickly and lift off the fat once chilled.
notes: Do not boil hard or the stock turns cloudy.
Food safety: cool within 2 hours, keep in the fridge up to 4 days or freeze for 3 months, and reheat until boiling hot. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Clear Fish Stock from Snapper Frames
recipes.summary: A light, sweet fish stock simmered only 25 minutes so it stays clean and clear.

items: 1 kg white fish frames, gills removed

steps: Rinse the fish frames well under cold water until the water runs clear.
Place everything in a pot, bring to a bare simmer and skim until the surface is clear.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes, no longer, until the fish flesh turns opaque and flakes and the stock is fragrant.
Strain through a fine sieve and cool quickly.
notes: Food safety: cool within 1 hour, keep in the fridge up to 2 days or freeze for 3 months.
Boiling or simmering past 30 minutes makes it bitter.

recipes.title: Ham Hock and Bay Bone Broth
recipes.summary: A smoky, collagen-rich broth from ham hock with bay, onion and peppercorns.
steps: Place the ham hock and vegetables in a large pot with the bay, peppercorns and vinegar and cover with cold water.
Bring to a bare simmer and skim, then cook gently for 3 hours until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the hock, pull off the meat and keep it for soup.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and cool.
notes: Taste before salting; ham hock stock is salty.
Food safety: cool within 2 hours, keep in the fridge up to 4 days, and reheat until boiling hot. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Roasted Carrot and Ginger Bisque
recipes.summary: Smooth, sweet carrot soup roasted until caramelised, with fresh ginger and a swirl of cream.
steps: Roast the carrots and onion with the oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and soft.
Simmer with the ginger and stock for 10 minutes until completely tender.
Blend until silky smooth, stir in the cream and salt, and reheat gently until steaming.
Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with chives.
notes: Use coconut cream for dairy-free.
Freezes well without the cream for 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Roasted Pumpkin and Coconut Bisque
recipes.summary: Velvety pumpkin soup roasted with garlic and finished with coconut cream and lime.
steps: Roast the pumpkin, onion and garlic with the oil at 200°C for 30 minutes until soft and browned.
Simmer with the stock for 5 minutes until hot.
Blend until smooth, stir in the coconut cream, lime juice and salt, and reheat until steaming.
Serve with a pinch of chilli.
notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free if the stock is.
Freezes well for 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Thick Cream of Mushroom Soup
recipes.summary: Earthy, creamy mushroom soup with browned mushrooms, thyme and a splash of cream.
steps: Fry the mushrooms in the butter over high heat for 8 minutes until golden and the liquid has gone.
Add the onion, garlic and thyme and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock gradually and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Blend half the soup until smooth, return to the pot and stir in the cream and salt until hot.
notes: Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.
Do not boil after adding the cream.

recipes.title: Sweet Corn Bisque with Chilli Oil
recipes.summary: Silky corn soup blended with potato and finished with a drizzle of chilli oil.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the corn, potato and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is very tender.
Blend until completely smooth and press through a sieve for extra silkiness.
Stir in the milk and salt, reheat until steaming and drizzle with chilli oil.
notes: Fresh sweetcorn off 4 cobs works well in summer.
Freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Cauliflower and Cheddar Bisque
recipes.summary: Creamy roasted cauliflower soup enriched with mature cheddar and a hint of mustard.
steps: Roast the cauliflower and onion with the oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and tender.
Simmer with the stock and milk for 8 minutes until hot.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cheddar and mustard until melted.
Season with the salt and reheat gently until steaming.
notes: Cheddar made with animal rennet is not suitable for vegetarians; choose a vegetarian cheddar.
Freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Kids' Chicken Noodle Soup for the Thermos
recipes.summary: A mild chicken soup with tiny noodles and soft vegetables, ideal for a school lunchbox thermos.
steps: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 12 minutes until cooked through with no pink, then lift out and shred.
Add the carrot, celery and pasta to the stock and simmer for 8 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Return the chicken with the peas and cook for 2 minutes until hot, then stir in the parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout; keep the soup above 60°C in the thermos by pre-heating it with boiling water, and eat within 4 hours.
Use low-salt stock for little ones.

recipes.title: Kids' Creamy Tomato Soup with Cheese Toast Dippers
recipes.summary: Smooth mild tomato soup with strips of cheesy toast for dunking.
steps: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 6 minutes until tender.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Blend until smooth and stir in the milk.
Top the bread with cheddar, grill for 3 minutes until bubbling, then cut into strips for dipping.
notes: Add a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes are sharp.
Freezes for 3 months.

recipes.title: Kids' Mild Veggie Minestrone for the Lunchbox
recipes.summary: A gentle vegetable and small pasta soup with no spice, perfect for a thermos.
steps: Soften the carrot, zucchini and celery in the oil for 5 minutes until tender.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the pasta and beans and simmer for 8 minutes until the pasta is tender, then add the parsley.
notes: Pre-heat the thermos with boiling water before filling.
Sprinkle a little vegetarian hard cheese over the top if you like.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Red Onions with Orange and Chilli
recipes.summary: Bright pink onions in an orange and cider vinegar brine, ready in 15 minutes for brunch plates.
steps: Pack the onions into a clean jar.
Warm the vinegar, orange juice, sugar, salt and chilli in a small pan for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the onions, press down until covered, and cool before using.
notes: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
Ready to eat after 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Carrot and Radish Ribbons
recipes.summary: Crisp, tangy carrot and radish ribbons that perk up avocado toast and eggs.
steps: Pack the carrot and radish into a clean jar.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar and salt for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the vegetables and cool until room temperature before covering.
notes: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
Great on rice bowls.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Cornbread Stuffing Muffins
recipes.summary: Cornmeal and sage stuffing baked into muffins with crisp tops, a gluten-free side for Thanksgiving.
steps: Dry the bread cubes at 150°C for 15 minutes until crisp.
Soften the onion and celery in the butter for 6 minutes until tender, then stir in the sage.
Toss the bread with the vegetables, stock, egg and salt until just moist.
Spoon into a greased muffin tin and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes until golden and set.
notes: Food safety: cook until the centre reaches 75°C because the mixture contains raw egg.
Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.

recipes.title: Maple Sweet Potatoes with Toasted Pecans
recipes.summary: Roasted sweet potato chunks glazed with maple syrup and sprinkled with pecans.

items: 1 kg sweet potatoes, cut into chunks

steps: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, cinnamon and salt and roast at 200°C for 30 minutes until tender and browned.
Drizzle with the maple syrup and roast for 8 minutes more until glossy and caramelised.
Scatter with the pecans and serve hot.
notes: Vegan and gluten-free.
Use walnuts if you prefer.

recipes.title: Sage Cornbread Dressing
recipes.summary: Savoury baked cornbread dressing with onion, celery and plenty of fresh sage.
steps: Soften the onion and celery in the butter for 8 minutes until tender, then stir in the sage.
Toss with the cornbread, stock, eggs and salt until well moistened.
Spoon into a greased dish and bake at 190°C for 35 minutes until golden on top and set.
notes: Food safety: bake until the centre reaches 75°C because of the raw egg.
Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.
